sources.citation: Clouse, Duane A. 1997. Towards a reconstruction and reclassification of the Lakes Plain languages of Irian Jaya. In Karl Franklin (ed.), Papers in Papuan linguistics No. 2 (Pacific Linguistics A-85), 133-236. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics, ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-A85.133; hdl:1885/253630.
sources.note: Papasena explicitly excluded from the study for lack of data (p.134); family-level only: p.152 'Tone is a prominent feature of all Lakes Plain languages... All the modern languages have at least high and low tone'; p.160 (Appendix 3 note) 'stress is not marked because only a few original word lists marked it and it has not been found to be contrastive in any of the Lakes Plain languages to date'. No Papasena wordlist in the appendix; Papasena appears only in the East Tariku tree (p.155).

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-B31; hdl:1885/146481.
sources.note: Checklist entry '84. PAPASENA, IXa, Village: Papasena, Source: U13' (U13 = missionary survey wordlists) and a 40-item comparative list '84. PAPASENA (Br)' in the appendix; no phonological notes, no stress or tone marks anywhere (the string 'stress' occurs nowhere in the volume).

sources.citation: Menanti, Jacqualine & Ben Rumaropen. 2022. Survey Report on the Kapauri Language of Papua, Indonesia. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-026. SIL International. 69 pp. Appendix B.4 (pp.41-48) = scanned handwritten 'Ari' (Papasena) wordlist, L. McAllister, Papasena village, 18 April 1986 (= McAllister 1986b, SIL archive 69145).
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey; the words stress/tone/accent/pitch never occur; p.23 says all appendix data are unanalysed field transcriptions. The scanned McAllister wordlist (viewed pp.41-42) carries a hand-written stress tick on most Papasena items, in varying positions (ˈtaɽu 'boil', aˈpu 'buttocks', akuˈta 'chest', ˈaikipu 'elbow', ˈawa 'eye', ˈkitawig 'ant', kwaˈaɽu 'fly', ˈkug 'tree'); no rule stated.

sources.citation: Yoder, Brendon. 2020. A grammar of Abawiri, a Lakes Plain language of Papua, Indonesia. PhD dissertation, UC Santa Barbara. Sections 1.3-1.4 (pp.9-12).
sources.note: About Papasena only that it is 'not mentioned in all Clouse's work' but always placed in East Tariku; the inventory of existing Lakes Plain descriptions (Iau, Doutai, Edopi, Obokuitai, Sikaritai, Kirikiri, Fayu, Abawiri) contains nothing on Papasena. Family remark: 'All of these languages are tonal'. Nothing on Papasena stress.
